subsection.name: PCI DSS - Payment Card Industry Security Standard
subsection.applies to: Applies to any merchant, service provider, or entity involved in processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data, regardless of size
controller requirements: Build and maintain a secure network
Protect cardholder data
Maintain a vulnerability management program
Implement strong access control measures
Regularly monitor and test networks
Maintain an information security policy

subsection.name: EU GDPR
subsection.applies to: Applies to businesses that process the personal data of EU citizens and residents or offer products or services to EU citizens
controller requirements: Processing must be lawful, fair, and transparent to the data subject
Must process data for the legitimate purposes specified explicitly to the data subject when you collected it
Colled and process only as must data as absolutely necessary for the purposes specified
Must keep personal data accurate and up to date
May only store personally identifying data for as long as necessary for the purposes specified
Processing must be done in such a way as to ensure appropriate security, integrity, and confidentiality
Data controller is responsible for being able to demonstrate GDPR compliance

Need a DPO if a public authority other than a court acting in a judicial capacity, core activities require you to monitor people systematically and regularly on a large scale, or core activities are large-scale processing of special categories of data listed under Article 9 of the GDPR or data relating to criminal convictions and offenses mentioned in Article 10
individual rights: must give specific, unambiguous consent to process the data
rights in relation to automated decision making and profiling
subsection.fines: up to 20 million euro or 4% of global revenue

subsection.name: Personal Information Protection Law - China
subsection.applies to: Applies to processing activities outside China if they involve providing products/services to individuals in China or analyzing their behavior
controller requirements: Transferring data outside China requires compliance with security assessments by the Cyberspace Administration of China
Processing requires, in most cases, explicit consent from the individual and must have a clear, reasonable purpose
Critical information infrastructure are required to store data within China
subsection.fines: can lead to severe penalties, including fines up to 50 million RMB or 5% of annual revenue, and potential suspension of business operations

subsection.name: LGPD - Brazil
subsection.applies to: Applies to any individual or legal entity processing data in Brazil, offering goods/services there, or collecting data within the country
controller requirements: Processing must be based on specific legal grounds, such as consent, contractual necessity, or legitimate interest
Organizations must appoint a DPO to oversee compliance and communicate with the National Data Protection Authority
must report security incidents that may create risk to data subjects within a reasonable time
individual rights: right to portability of their data

subsection.name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act - India
subsection.applies to: Applies to entities in India and international companies processing data of individuals in India or entities offering goods/services to individuals in India
controller requirements: Processing requires free, specific, informed, and unconditional consent
must implement security safeguards like encryption and data retention for only as long as necessary
Mandatory reporting of data breaches to the Data Protection Board and affected individuals, with detailed report within 72 hours

subsection.name: Federal Act on Data Protection - Switzerland
subsection.applies to: Applies to all organizations processing data of Swiss residents, enforcing strict rules on data handling, transparency, and security
controller requirements: Mandatory data breach notifications to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner, privacy by design/default, and data protection impact assessments
Stricter rules for transferring data outside Switzerland, requiring sufficient, comparable data protection in the destination country
subsection.fines: up to CHF 250,000 for intentional violations

subsection.name: Argentina Personal Data Protection Act - Argentina
subsection.applies to: Companies operating in Argentina or working with consumer data of Argentinians
controller requirements: Regulates the processing of personal data to protect privacy
Mandates purpose, proportionality, transparency, data accuracy, security, and confidentiality in all processing
Explicit, informed, and free consent is required for data collection
Strict protection applies to sensitive data
Transfers to countries with inadequate protection are restricted
individual rights: right to object to automated decisions and profiling

subsection.name: Privacy Act 1988 - Australia
subsection.applies to: Applies to entities over AU$3 million annual turnover and government agencies
controller requirements: must obtain consent to collect sensitive information and generally cannot use data for secondary purposes without consent
must report eligible data breaches to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner and affected individuals
individual rights: right to access their personal information
right to remain anonymous or use a pseudonym where practical

subsection.name: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act - Canada
subsection.applies to: Applies to private sector organizations including federally regulated businesses
controller requirements: required to obtain meaningful consent for data collection and use
Imposes stricter standards, including explicit opt in consent for data collection and significant penalties up to $25 million for breaches
must report breaches of security safeguards to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner and notify affected individuals

subsection.name: Law 1518 of 2021 - Colombia
subsection.applies to: Companies operating in Colombia or working with consumer data of Colombians
controller requirements: Explicit authorization is required from the data subject for collecting and processing data
Restrictions apply to transferring data outside of Colombia, generally requiring the receiving country to meet adequate data protection standards

subsection.name: Danish Data Protection Act - Denmark
subsection.applies to: Applies to both public and private sectors
controller requirements: Supplements the GDPR, providing stricter provisions on employee monitoring and specific rules for handling sensitive data
Regulates the processing of data relating to criminal offenses and civil registration numbers
Processing of personal data for personnel administration is allowed based on legitimate interests arising from legislation or collective agreements
Requires clear, active, and prior consent for using cookies
Data subjects must be informed without undue delay if a break is likely to result in high risk to their rights

subsection.name: Data Protection Act - Finland
subsection.applies to: Campnies operating in Finland or working wtih consumer data of Finland citizens
controller requirements: Supplements the GDPR by strictly regulating employee monitoring, background checks, and email access
Regulates cookies and requires informed consent for non essential tracking

subsection.name: French Data Protection Act - France
subsection.applies to: Applies to any entity processing personal data of French residents, whether established in France or not
controller requirements: Supplements the GDPR by providing specific rules for data processing, especially concerning sensitive data
Requires explicit, informed, and unambiguous consent for data collection, with specific rules for minors
Mandates clear privacy policies detailing data use, purposes, and data controller identity
Upholds GDPR rights
Adds provisions for sensitive data
inform the CNIL and affected individuals about breaches
Prohibits processing data revealing racial/ethnic origin, political/religious beliefs, or union affiliation unless specific conditions are met

subsection.name: German Federal Data Protection Act - Germany
subsection.applies to: Companies operating in German or working with consuemr data of Germans
controller requirements: Sets out specific regulations and guidelines concerning the collection, processing, and storage of personal data by both public and private entities operating within Germany’s jurisdiction
Data can only be collected and processed for specific, explicit, and legitimate purposes
Only the minimum amount of personal data necessary for the intended purposes can be collected and processed
Personal data must be accurate and where necessary kept up to data
Personal data should not be stored for longer than necessary for the purposes for which it was processed
Appropriate technical and organizational measures must be implemented to protect personal data from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction
Processing personal data through video surveillance requires additional justification and notification requirements
Profiling with potential for automated decision making requires transparency and right to object
individual rights: Right to information and access - data subjects have the right to obtain transparent information about the processing of their personal data
Right to rectification - data subjects have the right to request the rectification of inaccurate or incomplete personal data concerning them
Right to erasure - data subjects have the right to request the erasure of their personal data under certain circumstances
Right to restriction of processing - data subjects have the right to request the restriction of the processing of their personal data is specific situations

Right to data portability - data subjects have the right to receive their personal data in a structured, commonly used, and machine readable format and have the right to transmit that data to another data controller without hindrance from the original data controller

Right to object - data subjects have the right to object to the processing of their personal data, including processing based on legitimate interest pursued by the data controller or for direct marking purposes
Right to withdraw consent - where the processing of personal data is based on consent, data subjects have the right to withdraw their consent at any time

subsection.name: Law 4624/2019 - Greece
subsection.applies to: companies operating in Greece or working with consumer data of Greeks
controller requirements: Covers GDPR implementation
Personal data must only be kept for as long as necessary, though longer retention is permitted for scientific, historical, or statistical purposes
Strict regulations govern the processing of employee personal data
Data subject consent is required for marketing, with specific rules for recording, storing, and opting out

subsection.name: Act of Data Protection and the Processing of Personal Data - Iceland
subsection.applies to: Applies to both public and private sector
controller requirements: Implements the GDPR into Icelandic law
Organizations need to appoint a Data Protection Officer who must maintain confidentiality regarding information learned
must notify government and affected subjects of data breaches

subsection.name: Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law - Indonesia
subsection.applies to: Applies to any entity that processes the data of Indonesian residents or acts with legal consequences in Indonesia
controller requirements: Transfers of data outside Indonesia are permitted if the receiving country has an equal or higher level of protection, or if specific contractual clauses are met

subsection.name: Protection of Privacy Law - Israel
subsection.applies to: Companies operating in Israel or working with consumer data of Israel citizens
controller requirements: DPOs for certain entities and increased requirements for data security and breach notifications are required
Data collection requires informed, specific, and voluntary consent, particularly for sensitive data
Entities holding databases containing sensitive data, or large scale, automated, or marketing data, must register with the PPA
individual rights: right to delete or object to the use of their personal data in certain circumstances

subsection.name: Act on the Protection of Personal Information - Japan
subsection.applies to: Applies to any business handling the personal information of Japanese residents, even if the business is located outside of Japan
controller requirements: Prior consent is required to transfer data to third parties, with specific exceptions for joint use or mergers
Mandatory reporting to the PPC is required for significant breaches
individual rights: right to delete their personal data

subsection.name: Personal Data Protection Act - Malaysia
subsection.applies to: Applies to any person/entity that processes, or has control over the processing of personal data in respect of commercial transaction
controller requirements: Mandatory notification to the commissioner for data breaches that cause or are likely to cause significant harm
Companies must appoint a DPO
individual rights: right to correct their personal data
right to request that their data not be used for direct marketing
right to request their data be transferred to another data user

subsection.name: Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties - Mexico
subsection.applies to: Applies to any individual or entity in Mexico, and foreign companies processing data of Mexican residents
controller requirements: must obtain explicit consent for sensitive data, provide clear privacy notices, and implement strict security measures

subsection.name: Privacy Act 2020 - New Zealand
subsection.applies to: Applies to overseas organizations doing business in New Zealand
controller requirements: Organizations must notify the Commissioner and affected individuals of notifiable privacy breaches
Personal information can only be sent overseas if the recipient is subject to similar binding privacy laws
required to appoint a privacy officer to ensure compliance
individual rights: in some cases right to delete their personal information
subsection.fines: up to NZ$10,000 for specific offenses

subsection.name: Republic Act No 10173 - Philippines
subsection.applies to: Applies to any organization processing personal data of Philippine residents, whether in the Philippines or abroad, if it involves Philippine citizens or residents
individual rights: right to portability of their data

subsection.name: Federal Law No 152-FZ - Russia
subsection.applies to: Companies operating in Russia or working with consumer data of Russians
controller requirements: Requires that the initial recording, storage, and processing of Russian citizens’ personal data occur on databases located within the Russian Federation
Personal data processing generally requires explicit, informed, and specific consent
Data operators must notify government of data breaches within 24 hours of detection, and report investigation results within 72 hours
Transfers to countries that do not provide adequate protection require compliance with specific, strict conditions

subsection.name: Protection of Personal Information Act - South Africa
subsection.applies to: Applies to public and private bodies processing personal information within South Africa
controller requirements: Data processing must adhere to accountability, processing limitation, purpose specification, further processing limitation, information quality, openness, security safeguards, and data subject participation
individual rights: right to request the deletion of their personal

subsection.name: Organic Law 3/2018 - Spain
subsection.applies to: Companies operating in Spain or working with consumer data of Spaniards
controller requirements: Processing must have a valid basis, such as consent, contractual necessity, or legitimate interest
Consent for processing data of minors is valid from age 14

subsection.name: Data Protection Act - Sweden
subsection.applies to: Companies operating in Sweden or working with consumer data of Swedes
controller requirements: Supplements the GDPR
Personal identity numbers require special protection and their processing is strictly regulated
Only public authorities are generally permitted to process data relating to criminal convictions
Consent required for electronic direct marketing to individuals, though opt out is allowed for existing customers

subsection.name: Personal Data Protection Act - Thailand
subsection.applies to: Applies to organizations outside Thailand that process data of Thai residents, as well as businesses operating within the country
controller requirements: Organizations must obtain explicit consent to collect, sue, or disclose data, unless another lawful basis exists
Data must be only used for the stated purpose
Organizations that process sensitive data or require regular monitoring of data must appoint a DPO
In the event of a breach the DPO must inform the Personal Data Protection Committee within 72 hours
Transferring personal data outside of Thailand requires ensuring that the destination country or organization maintains adequate data protection standards
individual rights: right to restrict the use of their personal data
subsection.fines: There are fines for non compliance

subsection.name: Law No 18.331 - Uruguay
subsection.applies to: Companies that operate in Uruguay or work with consumer data of Uruguaians
controller requirements: All databases containing personal data must be registered
Breaches must be reported to the URCDP within 72 hours
Uruguay is deemed adequate by the EU meaning personal data can be transferred from the EU to Uruguay without additional safeguards
DPOs are required for public entities, organizations processing sensitive data, and those managing data of over 35,000 individuals
Data processing requires informed, unequivocal, and express consent of the data subject
Data must be collected for a specific, legitimate purpose
